narrative:
By dusk, a guild office is shuttered and a notice has been nailed across its door: UNFAIR CROWN LEVIES BLEED THE ROAD. A bell-ringer named Tamsin leans under the awning, pretending not to wait for anyone.

@Tamsin: I hear the guilds are planning a petition. I also hear they bought enough arrows for a war. One of those is probably true.

narrative:
Auditor Cassin Hollis does not look up from his ledger. @Cassin: The large guilds pay once at the capital and pass the cost downward. Small carriers pay at every gate. The crown calls it efficiency. The road calls it starvation.

He closes the ledger. @Cassin: Knowing the arithmetic will not make the next choice cleaner.

narrative:
Three days later, the petition has become a crowd outside the levy house. Guildmistress Yeva Solt demands a hearing. Bailiff Corin Reyes answers with a statute book and a line of guards. Petra Voss watches Yeva from the edge of the square, calculating.

There is still time for words to matter.

narrative: For one long hour, neither side leaves the room. When the doors open, the levy is suspended for the winter and a review is promised in spring. It is not justice. It is enough to stop the square from burning tonight.

narrative: At dawn, someone rings the Salt Road bell until the rope snaps. Barricades close the gate. Captain-Reeve Osgar Vell gives the crowd one order to disperse. No one moves. Corin Reyes looks from his guards to the families behind the barricade, and for the first time cannot find a statute that makes the moment smaller.

narrative: Your words do not make anyone happy. They make enough people afraid of the next minute to put weapons down. The crown accepts a written concession under witness; the guilds accept that the gate will remain standing.
